recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

reccbsotzqb82K2Zv.Bio: Josh Bigelsen, along with his brother Adam, continues the work of their father Dr. Harvey Bigelsen, analyzing what they call "holographic" fractal patterns in dark-field blood microscopy to reveal emotional and physical health information, in line with terrain-theory (pleomorphism) views of biology.
reccbsotzqb82K2Zv.Name: Josh Bigelsen

reco9VwyEs3ndBR8J.Bio: Adam Bigelsen co-founded the Bigelsen Academy with his brother Josh, continuing their father Dr. Harvey Bigelsen's terrain-theory work, and teaches the "Holographic Blood" method of reading disturbance patterns in blood tied to physical and emotional health.
reco9VwyEs3ndBR8J.Name: Adam Bigelsen

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Honest Microscopy Versus Viral Nanotech Claims", "body": "Opening the extension, Chance asks what gets repeated online without anyone doing the work, and the brothers go straight to the dark field images being passed around. Adam recalls a doctor in Guadalajara claiming total knowledge from two years of watching videos, and compares that to reading a bike manual without ever riding. Josh explains that a dark field microscope cannot resolve nanoparticles, and the brothers note that supposed graphene photos match images printed in books over a century old, while a drop of plain saline on a slide yields the same salt crystals being sold as nano circuitry. Falsified evidence, they argue, discredits everyone."}, {"title": "Shaking Off Fear Like a Rabbit", "body": "The brothers frame healing as a switch between sympathetic and parasympathetic states. A rabbit tenses when it senses a coyote, then shakes the tension off once the predator is gone, while people keep carrying what a parent yelled at age ten or what a teacher said at nine. From there the talk turns on the word accident. The brothers insist there is no such thing and ask Chance for a better word, and he offers incident, since you need to see in yourself what it was. Chance then describes accepting his own fear in March 2020 and argues the key inversion is believing effects come before consciousness."}, {"title": "What Soil Teaches About Supplements", "body": "Regenerative agriculture becomes a mirror for the body. Farmers who fed plants from above found they stopped forming mycorrhizal connections and grew shallow roots, and livestock given minerals in their feed stopped eating the wild plants that carried them, which the brothers compare to taking vitamin C instead of eating an orange. Chance adds that he quit supplementing vitamin D after learning it acts like a hormone, and raises Matt Powers' view of bacteria as a universal chassis. A Spanish farmer's green land, surrounded by brown tilled fields, is summed up in his words: my soil is too strong. Suppressed strep, the brothers warn, simply morphs into something worse."}, {"title": "Regeneration Follows Love, Not Fear", "body": "Nature returns once the blockage is removed. The brothers describe a Mexican project that regenerated tens of thousands of desert acres without planting a seed, simply by reintroducing wildlife, and a California river where the salmon and steelhead run came back within two years of a dam coming down. Chance adds reports of record monsoons and unexpected creatures in Arizona after a friend spread orgone devices, and frames it all on an axis of love versus fear, where fear narrows what we can perceive. Adam relays scientist Anna Maria's prescription to take off your shoes, hug a tree and get some joy, then write ten joys and do one daily."}, {"title": "Holograms in the Eye and Hidden Poisons", "body": "Chance asks whether the eye, and the I am, might be the key to a holographic reality. The brothers answer that practitioners who read the iris, tongue, ear or foot are reading the same energetic disturbance they see in blood, formed much like echolocation. They recall the head of hematology at Tufts refusing to look at their father's live, unstained blood. Chance then proposes that virology may covertly be the study of poisons and venoms, noting the word's roots in animal venom. The brothers bring in homotoxicology, a six phase chart showing how suppressing each symptom with another drug drives illness deeper, from bacterial healing toward fungal decomposition."}]
